thread.title: Intraday Update: Dow Drops 130 Points as Too Much Bad News Lifts Dollar - Barron's

author: Brett Arends
title: Intraday Update: Dow Drops 130 Points as Too Much Bad News Lifts Dollar - Barron's
text:
By Brett Arends Updated May 23, 2018 1:42 p.m. ET Yikes! The dollar jumped 1% to a five-month high Wednesday morning, following negative political and economic news out of Europe. And that might help explain why the Dow Jones Industrial Average is lower.
Illustration: Getty Images The Dow Jones Industrial Average was off 150 points by early afternoon, while the broader Standard & Poor’s 500 was down about half a percent. Small-caps were firmer, with the Russell 2000 rising about 0.25%. About as many stocks rose as fell. Retail stocks were under pressure after Target 's (TGT) earnings miss .
The U.S. Dollar Index is now up a remarkable 10% in just over a month. The euro briefly fell below $1.17 Wednesday morning, while the British pound is down to $1.33—not far above the level it hit just after the Brexit shock two years ago .
The moves follow the latest purchasing managers’ index data from the European Union , which came in below forecasts and suggest the economies there are weaker than some had thought. French unemployment figures also came in higher than expected, though when you count all the people who are busy rioting in Paris , the numbers probably look a lot better.
Some headlines also blame new worries about Italian politics, where the latest negotiations over the formation of a new populist government have hit another snag. Italian bond yields have surged at the same time.
Alas and alack, Italian politics are almost always in a mess —and Italian government bond yields, remarkably, are still a long way below those of the U.S.
President Donald Trump has raised the chance that his forthcoming meeting with North Korea’s leader may not happen. Yet South Korea’s Kospi index actually rose 0.26% overnight.
Among the most popular stocks, Facebook (FB) was 1.1% higher by early afternoon and Netflix (NFLX) 1.9%. Apple (AAPL) edged up 0.2% and Tesla (TSLA) 0.4%, while Amazon.com (AMZN) was 0.7% better and Alphabet (GOOGL) 0.5%.
S&P 500 : -0.3% to 2715.89
Dow 30 : -131.4 points, or 0.5%, to 24,703.01
Nasdaq : -0.1% to 7374.58
Vix : +1.7% to 13.45
10-year Treasury Yield : -0.05 percentage point to 3.02%
Midday Movers Booking Holdings (BKNG) is down 0.6% to $2,065.65 on news that Russia is considering a ban on the online travel agency.
Ctrip.com (CTRP) is up 4.5% to $45.40 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The online travel agency said it earned 55 cents a share on revenue of $1.08 billion. Analysts were looking for 16 cents a share in earnings on revenue $1.05 billion.
Casino stocks are falling after casino workers in Las Vegas voted to strike . Las Vegas Sands (LVS) down 0.7% to 78.43, MGM Resorts (MGM), down 0.9% to $31.30, and Wynn Resorts (WYNN) down 0.7% to $192.49.
Papa John's International (PZZA) is up 3.1% to $52.78 on ongoing M&A speculation.
Red Robin Gourmet Burgers (RRGB) is down 17.7% to $47.76 following its first-quarter earnings . The restaurant earned 69 cents a share on revenue of $421.5 million. Analysts were looking for earnings of 76 cents on revenue of $427.01 million. For the second quarter, it expects to earn between 55 cents and 75 cents a share, compared with the 75 cent per-share consensus. — Teresa Rivas
